newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - KDB takes French francs.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - KDB takes French francs.

text.p: Asian debt markets ended the week quietly, with Korea Development Bank's French franc deal the day's major transaction.
KDB launched via Societe Generale a 5.625 percent 1.5 billion French franc six-year bond at 99.771 to yield 33 basis points over comparable French government paper.
Among other South Korean issuers, a senior official at state-owned Korea Container Terminal Co said the company may increase its samurai bond issues to about 10 billion yen or more starting in 1997.
Korean Container is scheduled to launch its first samurai bond issue next week. The deal is expected to be five billion yen in size and have a duration of five years.
In other new issues, India's Videocon has mandated Peregrine Fixed Income to arrange a seven-year US$70 million floating rate note issue, the borrower's first.
Like other deals structured by Peregrine, this one will be launched with an indicated spread rather than a set spread.
The indicated spread has not been decided, but the issue is expected to pay more than 200 basis points over LIBOR. Roadshows start in Asia on October 14.
Taiwan's Lite-On Technology Corp said it would issue US$45 million in floating rate notes to finance bank loan repayments.
The five-year notes will pay an all-in return of LIBOR plus 82 basis points and will be launched in late November or early December, the company said.
Citicorp International, one of the most active arrangers of Taiwan issues, is expected to run the books on the Lite-On deal.
Arranger China Development Finance Co today released the names of the 61 banks that participated in Bank of China Hong Kong branch's inaugural LAF-eligible FRCD issue.

Eligibility for LAF, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window, makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
The Bank of China issue was raised to HK$4 billion after being 4.5 times oversubscribed from its initial HK$2 billion amount to HK$9 billion.
Another Hong Kong dollar issue, an FRCD for Asia Commercial Bank, was increased to HK$550 million from HK$500 million.
